thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — Dedicated pool 'xenith-pool' high GPU util (100%) and request errors for tenant XenithCorp. 503s observed. Paging on-call.

sara.m: I'm on it — on-call SRE. Observing sustained 100% GPU util on all 4 nodes in xenith-pool. Latency spike + queue growth reported by runtime.

mike: seeing same on dashboards. Error spike started at ~2310003500. Tenant rate looks normal but token churn high (long context).

aditya: adding context — Xenith recently rolled a large batch of long-context evals at ~2309999000, might be prefix cache miss.

sara.m: can we confirm isolation? Are other tenants impacted?

mike: checking multi-tenant metrics -> other tenants on the host machines show normal utilization ~30-50%. This is isolated to xenith pool and traffic from XenithCorp.

aditya: looks like request concurrency + long seq lengths are causing KV cache thrash and continuous batching backlog.

ops-bot: autoscaler event: pool xenith-pool targeted min=4 max=4 (burst disabled). No additional GPUs will be provisioned automatically.

sara.m: ah — dedicated pool has burst disabled per contract. That explains no autoscale. Can we enable temporary burst? Who can change policy?

kevin-prod: sales/engineering agreed to no burst for cost predictability. CSM should approve emergency burst. @julia.csm can you confirm outreach and permission to burst?

julia.csm: on it. Pinged Xenith support contact (x-support@xenithcorp). Waiting ack. We have emergency clause for critical outages.

mike: mitigation options listing:
1) Enable burst / increase pool to 8 GPUs (fastest but contract/approval needed).
2) Divert Xenith traffic to a hosted fallback model (may change response characteristics).
3) Throttle/limit longest-context requests at ingress (rate-limit heavy calls).
4) Spin up a temporary private pool and migrate heavy sessions (longer).

aditya: also can we roll a quantized model variant with lower memory to reduce KV pressure? Build + warmup time ~10-20m.

sara.m: recommend immediate mitigation 1 + 3: request emergency burst to 8 GPUs + apply short-term ingress throttle for requests > 8k tokens. That should relieve queues while model variant builds.

incident-bot: ACTION created: #INC-2310004567-EMERGENCY-BURST assigned to sara.m, mike.

julia.csm: Xenith contact replied: "We are seeing major service degradation — please proceed with emergency steps now." Written approval received.

kevin-prod: noted. Proceed but keep billing/CS aware.

sara.m: executing: enabling burst on xenith-pool -> ops API call: `POST /pools/xenith-pool/burst?target=8`

ops-bot: API accepted, request queued to provision 4 GPUs in region us-west-2. Estimated time ~5m.

mike: applying quick ingress rate-limit rule to tenant XenithCorp: `xrd-config set rate_limit xenith tenant_token_prefix: 100r/s max_seq_len: 8000`

aditya: starting build of quantized model variant (q4_0) for Xenith workload. warming caches.

~5m later~

ops-bot: 4 GPUs provisioned and added to xenith-pool. Pool size now 8.

mike: GPU util dropped to ~55% across pool, request queue drained, 503s stopped. Latency returning to normal for most requests.

sara.m: confirmed mitigation working. Traffic stabilized. Continuing to monitor for 15m.

julia.csm: told Xenith support: "We've provisioned emergency capacity and applied short-term limits. Your traffic should normalize; we'll follow up with a postmortem and options for capacity/contract changes."

kevin-prod: flagging for auto-bill override discussion later — do not invoice emergency burst until follow-up.

aditya: quantized variant warmed, starting canary traffic at 10% to reduce KV pressure and evaluate output parity.

mike: canary looks good so far. If stable, we can keep q-variant as fallback to reduce baseline cost.

sara.m: handoff to next on-call in 10m — @mike will monitor the rest of the window.

mike: taking over monitoring. Will keep this thread updated. Current status: mitigated, monitoring.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATE -> MITIGATED. Severity: Sev2 (customer-impacting, single-tenant). Follow-up required: RCA, contract review for burst policy, alert tuning for long-context runs, and a playbook update for emergency authorization flow.

sara.m: local notes for RCA: root cause = dedicated pool burst disabled + unexpected long-sequence workload from Xenith causing sustained KV/cpu/gpu pressure. Action items assigned in ticket INC-2310004567.

julia.csm: scheduling customer call in 2h to review.

kevin-prod: please include cost/impact estimates in post-incident brief.

mike: logging final metrics and closing pager. Will add transcripts and dashboards link to ticket.

sara.m: thanks team.

aditya: follow-up: propose automated per-tenant warning at 80% pool util + pre-authorized mini-burst (1-2 GPUs) for enterprise contracts with consent flow.

julia.csm: +1. we'll surface that in contract templates.

mike: closing thread but keeping incident ticket open for RCA and action items.
